scenes.say: A supreme leader killed.
The world's most important oil route, choked.
And a region still on the edge.
This is the Iran war, from the first strike to today.
scenes.title: The Iran war, explained

scenes.say: The road to war was long.
scenes.title: Years in the making

scenes.say: In 2018, the US walked out of the nuclear deal.
In June 2025, Israel and Iran fought the 12-Day War.
scenes.speak: In June twenty twenty-five, Israel and Iran fought the twelve-day war.

scenes.say: It ended when US bunker-buster bombs hit Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan.
scenes.title: US strikes on nuclear sites

scenes.say: Then Iran's currency collapsed, and protests swept the country.
On 8 January, security forces opened fire.
scenes.speak: On the eighth of January, security forces opened fire.

scenes.say: Officials in Iran's own health ministry put the dead at 30,000 or more.
scenes.label: Killed in the January crackdown, per Iranian health officials
scenes.speak: Officials in Iran's own health ministry put the dead at thirty thousand or more.

scenes.say: Then America began its biggest build-up in the region since 2003.
scenes.speak: Then America began its biggest build-up in the region since two thousand and three.

scenes.say: On 28 February, the US and Israel struck: nearly 900 strikes in 12 hours.
scenes.label: US and Israeli strikes in the first 12 hours
scenes.speak: On the twenty-eighth of February, the US and Israel struck: nearly nine hundred strikes in twelve hours.

scenes.say: Missiles, air defences, and Iran's leadership.
The first wave killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.
One strike hit a girls' school near Bandar Abbas. About 170 people died.
scenes.speak: One strike hit a girls' school near Bandar Abbas. About a hundred and seventy people died.

scenes.say: But the regime didn't collapse. It hardened.
Security chief Ali Larijani ran the country. Then, on 17 March, he too was killed.
scenes.speak: Security chief Ali Larijani ran the country. Then, on the seventeenth of March, he too was killed.

scenes.say: His son Mojtaba became supreme leader. The Revolutionary Guards took charge of the war.
Iran hit back across the region: Israel, and US bases from Iraq to the UAE.
scenes.title: Missiles across the Gulf

scenes.say: The aim: make the war too costly to continue.
On day two, drones hit Dubai airport. Flights across the Gulf stopped.
And in late March, Yemen's Houthis opened another front.
Then came the real battle: the Strait of Hormuz, the channel for a fifth of the world's oil.
Traffic fell by more than 90 per cent.
scenes.label: Commercial traffic through Hormuz
scenes.speak: Traffic fell by more than ninety per cent.

scenes.say: Iran let some ships through, on its own routes, for a heavy toll. In May, it set up an authority to run the strait.
Oil jumped from about 70 dollars a barrel to an average of 103 in March.
scenes.speak: Oil jumped from about seventy dollars a barrel to an average of a hundred and three in March.

scenes.say: Parts of Asia faced fuel shortages. India felt the squeeze.
Hezbollah joined from Lebanon. By late March, more than 11 lakh people had fled.
scenes.label: Displaced in Lebanon by late March
scenes.speak: Hezbollah joined from Lebanon. By late March, more than eleven lakh people had fled.

scenes.say: In April, Trump posted a threat.
scenes.text: "A whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again."

scenes.say: Within hours, he agreed to a ceasefire.
Pakistan brokered it. But talks failed, and the US blockaded Iran's ports.
scenes.title: April to July

scenes.say: In Islamabad, JD Vance met Iran's speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf: the highest-level contact since 1979.
scenes.speak: In Islamabad, J D Vance met Iran's speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf: the highest-level contact since nineteen seventy-nine.

scenes.say: In June, a deal to end the war. In July, it collapsed.
On 6 and 7 July, Iran struck three ships on a US-recommended route. Trump declared the truce over.
scenes.speak: On the sixth and seventh of July, Iran struck three ships on a U S recommended route. Trump declared the truce over.

scenes.say: In one week, US forces carried out more than 300 strikes.
scenes.label: US strikes in one week of July, on about 140 targets
scenes.speak: In one week, US forces carried out more than three hundred strikes.

scenes.say: Two American soldiers were killed in Jordan. Iran suspended the deal.
The toll, by official counts.
scenes.title: By official counts

scenes.say: The true figures are likely higher.
The fighting eased in August. The US says it has cleared Iran's mines and opened a corridor along Oman's coast.
Now, Gulf oil exports are back near prewar levels. But tankers are still being hit.
More than twice as much oil now moves by pipeline, around the strait.
And with elections in Israel and the US days away, the threats are getting louder.
This week, Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish envoys flew to Tehran to stop a new round.
scenes.text: Envoys in Tehran | to stop a new round

scenes.say: For India, one question: will the oil keep flowing?
